name: manual_482aa0
claim: Never call loop.stop() directly from inside an asyncio background task while asyncio.run()'s own top-level future is still pending; signal shutdown via an asyncio.Event and await asyncio.wait({main_task, stop_task}, return_when=FIRST_COMPLETED) instead, then cancel/cleanup gracefully.

decisions.notes: exa-mcp-daemon.py's _read_backend called asyncio.get_event_loop().stop() on backend stdout EOF, racing asyncio.run()'s pending future and raising 'RuntimeError: Event loop stopped before Future completed'. The shared Exa MCP daemon (orama-system/PT/Codex singleton multiplexer) crash-looped on every backend restart from ~2026-08-22 until fixed 2026-10-13 (orama PR #400). A second latent bug (ProcessLookupError on self.proc.terminate() when the backend already exited) only surfaced once this fix made the cleanup path reachable -- a reminder that fixing the first bug in a crash path can expose a second one in the same path.
